Reason: Security review SR-2025-14 of the pilot found that a stored refresh token let a stolen browser profile keep access for months. The team chose a one-week access token and no refresh token, so a stolen token expires on its own. Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: Sessions use one long-lived access token and the API has no refresh tokens.

@graph.pulse:content:
Password reset links stay valid for 30 minutes.
The API has no password reset flow yet. This fixes the rule for when it is built: a reset link works once and expires 30 minutes after it is sent.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Support tickets showed that users open a reset mail within 10 minutes. A link that lives 30 minutes covers slow mail delivery without leaving a long-lived link in an inbox. Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: Password reset links stay valid for 30 minutes.

@graph.pulse:content:
The fancyhash package is not used for password hashing because of its licence.
Password hashing stays on passlib with bcrypt. The fancyhash package was evaluated and rejected.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: The licence of fancyhash has a network-use clause that is not compatible with distributing the API. Passlib with bcrypt was kept. Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: The fancyhash package is not used for password hashing because of its licence.

@graph.pulse:content:
When the token fails to decode, or its username does not exist, the dependency raises HTTP 403 with MALFORMED_PAYLOAD. A wrong header prefix also returns 403.
Source: app/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py:90
@graph.pulse:title: An undecodable token or an unknown token user returns 403, not 401.

@graph.pulse:content: Cookie transport would need CSRF protection that this API does not have (ADR-5). Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: Tokens travel only in the Authorization header and never in cookies.

@graph.pulse:content:
Tokens are JWTs signed and verified with HS256. The secret comes from the application settings.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11
@graph.pulse:title: Access tokens are signed with the HS256 algorithm using one shared secret key.

@graph.pulse:content:
The register route checks the username first and the email second. Each taken value raises a 400 error with its own message from the strings module.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:70
@graph.pulse:title: Registering with a username or email that is already taken is answered with HTTP 400.

@graph.pulse:content:
queries is built by aiosql.from_path over the sql folder with the asyncpg adapter. Repositories call these named queries directly.
Source: app/app/db/queries/queries.py:5
@graph.pulse:title: Database queries are raw SQL files loaded with aiosql on the asyncpg driver, not an ORM.

@graph.pulse:content:
Queries are hand-written SQL files, not generated by an ORM.
Every query lives in a SQL file that the repositories call by name.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: The DBA team reviews every query. A SQL file can be reviewed in a pull request and ORM output cannot (ADR-4). Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: Queries are hand-written SQL files, not generated by an ORM.

@graph.pulse:content:
Both pool bounds default to 10 in the application settings, and the pool is created with those two values at start-up.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:22
@graph.pulse:title: The database pool is fixed at 10 connections through min_connection_count and max_connection_count.

@graph.pulse:content:
The token payload holds the username plus an expiry and the subject value access, which is a constant in the JWT service.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:10
@graph.pulse:title: Every access token carries the fixed subject claim access.

@graph.pulse:content: Product decision PD-8 puts all notifications out of scope until the 2027 roadmap. Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: Favoriting an article sends no notification to its author.

@graph.pulse:content: The DBA team reviews every query. A SQL file can be reviewed in a pull request and ORM output cannot (ADR-4). Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: Queries are hand-written SQL files, not generated by an ORM.

@graph.pulse:content:
convert_datetime_to_realworld replaces tzinfo with UTC and swaps +00:00 for Z. It replaces rather than converts the timezone, so it assumes values are already UTC.
Source: app/app/models/domain/rwmodel.py:7
@graph.pulse:title: Datetimes are serialized as UTC ISO strings ending in Z.

@graph.pulse:content:
The token payload holds only the username plus exp and sub. The current user is loaded by get_user_by_username, so a username change makes older tokens fail to resolve.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:29
@graph.pulse:title: The token identifies the user by username, not by numeric id.

@graph.pulse:content: Design review DR-31 found that the mobile list screen fits 20 rows without scrolling. Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: The article list defaults to 20 items per page.

@graph.pulse:content:
RWModel sets alias_generator to convert_field_to_camel_case and allows population by field name. Renaming a Python field changes the JSON key.
Source: app/app/models/domain/rwmodel.py:21
@graph.pulse:title: API field names are camelCase aliases generated from snake_case model fields.

@graph.pulse:content: Load test LT-9 put the login endpoint at a p95 of 240 ms with the default factor. One step higher pushed it past the 300 ms login budget. Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: bcrypt keeps the default passlib work factor.

@graph.pulse:content:
ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES is 60 * 24 * 7, and create_access_token_for_user uses it as the expiry delta. There is no refresh token in the code.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:12
@graph.pulse:title: Access tokens expire one week after issue.

@graph.pulse:content:
bcrypt keeps the default passlib work factor.
No custom rounds value is set on the password context, so passlib's default applies.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Load test LT-9 put the login endpoint at a p95 of 240 ms with the default factor. One step higher pushed it past the 300 ms login budget. Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: bcrypt keeps the default passlib work factor.

@graph.pulse:content:
The article list defaults to 20 items per page.
The default limit of the article list is 20 items.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Design review DR-31 found that the mobile list screen fits 20 rows without scrolling. Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: The article list defaults to 20 items per page.

@graph.pulse:content:
The migration creates a plpgsql function that sets NEW.updated_at = now(), with BEFORE UPDATE triggers on users, articles and commentaries.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:27
@graph.pulse:title: updated_at is maintained by a PostgreSQL trigger, not by application code.

@graph.pulse:content: Support tickets showed that users open a reset mail within 10 minutes. A link that lives 30 minutes covers slow mail delivery without leaving a long-lived link in an inbox. Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: Password reset links stay valid for 30 minutes.

@graph.pulse:content:
update_user assigns each field with `new or old`. An empty string or None leaves the stored value unchanged.
Source: app/app/db/repositories/users.py:64
@graph.pulse:title: User updates keep the old value when a field is empty, so bio cannot be cleared.

@graph.pulse:content: The data is relational, and the DBA team supports only PostgreSQL (ADR-3). Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: PostgreSQL is the data store and MongoDB was not chosen.

@graph.pulse:content:
A separate handler catches validation errors and answers with the validator's own error list, not the single detail string used for other HTTP errors.
Source: app/app/api/errors/validation_error.py:17
@graph.pulse:title: Request validation failures return HTTP 422 with an errors list of the validator's error objects.

@graph.pulse:content:
The header is split on one space and the prefix must equal settings.jwt_token_prefix, which defaults to Token. Any other prefix is rejected with 403.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:29
@graph.pulse:title: The Authorization header must use the prefix Token, not Bearer.

change_password generates a new bcrypt salt, stores it in the salt column, and hashes salt + password. check_password must prepend the same stored salt, so the salt column cannot be dropped.
Source: app/app/models/domain/users.py:24
@graph.pulse:title: A separate per-user salt is stored and prepended to the password before hashing.

@graph.pulse:content:
The login route looks up the user by email. Both a missing user and a failed password check raise the same wrong_login_error with INCORRECT_LOGIN_INPUT.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:30
@graph.pulse:title: Login uses email and returns one generic 400 error for unknown email and wrong password.

@graph.pulse:content:
The service compares the article author's username with the current user's username. Other users get a refusal.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23
@graph.pulse:title: Only an article's author, matched by username, may modify the article.

@graph.pulse:content: Legal review LR-77 requires that content its author deleted is gone from live storage within 24 hours. A deleted_at column was rejected because the rows would stay in the table. Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: Deleted articles and comments are removed from the database, with no soft-delete flag.

@graph.pulse:content:
Deleted articles and comments are removed from the database, with no soft-delete flag.
Deleting an article or a comment runs a SQL DELETE. No deleted_at column exists.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Legal review LR-77 requires that content its author deleted is gone from live storage within 24 hours. A deleted_at column was rejected because the rows would stay in the table. Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: Deleted articles and comments are removed from the database, with no soft-delete flag.

@graph.pulse:content:
The tags table has a single tag Text primary key, and articles_to_tags references tags.tag directly with cascade delete.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:124
@graph.pulse:title: Tags are stored by their text as the primary key, with no numeric id.

@graph.pulse:content:
DEFAULT_ARTICLES_LIMIT is 20 and DEFAULT_ARTICLES_OFFSET is 0. The query parameters enforce limit ge=1 and offset ge=0, with no maximum limit.
Source: app/app/models/schemas/articles.py:8
@graph.pulse:title: Article lists default to 20 items with limit at least 1 and no upper bound.

@graph.pulse:content: The licence of fancyhash has a network-use clause that is not compatible with distributing the API. Passlib with bcrypt was kept. Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: The fancyhash package is not used for password hashing because of its licence.

@graph.pulse:content:
A passlib CryptContext with the bcrypt scheme hashes and verifies passwords. deprecated is set to auto.
Source: app/app/services/security.py:4
@graph.pulse:title: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt through passlib.

@graph.pulse:content:
The create route builds the slug from the title and checks whether an article with that slug exists. If it does, the route raises a 400 error and does not add a numeric suffix.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:65
@graph.pulse:title: Creating an article whose generated slug already exists is refused with HTTP 400.

@graph.pulse:content:
A helper returns a fresh bcrypt salt as text. The user row stores the salt next to the hashed password.
Source: app/app/services/security.py:8
@graph.pulse:title: Each user gets a random salt created with bcrypt.gensalt.

@graph.pulse:content:
list_articles sets articles_count to len(articles) after applying limit and offset. Clients cannot get a total count from this field.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:49
@graph.pulse:title: articlesCount in list responses is the length of the returned page, not the total matching count.

@graph.pulse:content: Security review SR-2025-14 of the pilot found that a stored refresh token let a stolen browser profile keep access for months. The team chose a one-week access token and no refresh token, so a stolen token expires on its own. Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: Sessions use one long-lived access token and the API has no refresh tokens.

@graph.pulse:content:
Tokens travel only in the Authorization header and never in cookies.
The API reads the token from the Authorization header. It does not set or read any cookie.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Cookie transport would need CSRF protection that this API does not have (ADR-5). Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: Tokens travel only in the Authorization header and never in cookies.

Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:22
@graph.pulse:title: The asyncpg pool defaults to a fixed size of 10 connections.

@graph.pulse:content:
Favoriting an article sends no notification to its author.
Adding a favorite writes a database row and nothing else. No message is sent to the author.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Product decision PD-8 puts all notifications out of scope until the 2027 roadmap. Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: Favoriting an article sends no notification to its author.

@graph.pulse:content:
get_slug_for_article returns slugify(title). The slug is regenerated when the title changes on update, and it is the article URL key.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:19
@graph.pulse:title: An article slug is derived from its title with slugify.

@graph.pulse:content:
Sessions use one long-lived access token and the API has no refresh tokens.
The API issues a single access token that is valid for one week and has no refresh endpoint. A client that needs a new token logs in again.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Security review SR-2025-14 of the pilot found that a stored refresh token let a stolen browser profile keep access for months. The team chose a one-week access token and no refresh token, so a stolen token expires on its own. Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: Sessions use one long-lived access token and the API has no refresh tokens.

@graph.pulse:content:
Password reset links stay valid for 30 minutes.
The API has no password reset flow yet. This fixes the rule for when it is built: a reset link works once and expires 30 minutes after it is sent.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Support tickets showed that users open a reset mail within 10 minutes. A link that lives 30 minutes covers slow mail delivery without leaving a long-lived link in an inbox. Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: Password reset links stay valid for 30 minutes.

@graph.pulse:content:
The fancyhash package is not used for password hashing because of its licence.
Password hashing stays on passlib with bcrypt. The fancyhash package was evaluated and rejected.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: The licence of fancyhash has a network-use clause that is not compatible with distributing the API. Passlib with bcrypt was kept. Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: The fancyhash package is not used for password hashing because of its licence.

@graph.pulse:content:
When the token fails to decode, or its username does not exist, the dependency raises HTTP 403 with MALFORMED_PAYLOAD. A wrong header prefix also returns 403.
Source: app/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py:90
@graph.pulse:title: An undecodable token or an unknown token user returns 403, not 401.

@graph.pulse:content: Cookie transport would need CSRF protection that this API does not have (ADR-5). Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: Tokens travel only in the Authorization header and never in cookies.

@graph.pulse:content:
Tokens are JWTs signed and verified with HS256. The secret comes from the application settings.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11
@graph.pulse:title: Access tokens are signed with the HS256 algorithm using one shared secret key.

@graph.pulse:content:
The register route checks the username first and the email second. Each taken value raises a 400 error with its own message from the strings module.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:70
@graph.pulse:title: Registering with a username or email that is already taken is answered with HTTP 400.

@graph.pulse:content:
queries is built by aiosql.from_path over the sql folder with the asyncpg adapter. Repositories call these named queries directly.
Source: app/app/db/queries/queries.py:5
@graph.pulse:title: Database queries are raw SQL files loaded with aiosql on the asyncpg driver, not an ORM.

@graph.pulse:content:
Queries are hand-written SQL files, not generated by an ORM.
Every query lives in a SQL file that the repositories call by name.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: The DBA team reviews every query. A SQL file can be reviewed in a pull request and ORM output cannot (ADR-4). Invented for this demo.
@graph.pulse:title: Queries are hand-written SQL files, not generated by an ORM.

@graph.pulse:content:
Both pool bounds default to 10 in the application settings, and the pool is created with those two values at start-up.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:22
@graph.pulse:title: The database pool is fixed at 10 connections through min_connection_count and max_connection_count.

Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:10
@graph.pulse:title: Every access token carries the fixed subject claim access.
